addendum: Wikipedia-led tests, addendum q: do the book and author Wikipedia pages still help once the library model has 5 years of loans? (Letter p is taken by the scoring-only folder p_compare.)
status: Fixed 2026-11-26 15:15 +07:00 (08:15 UTC), before any step of it ran: the new model HM60 has not been fitted, nothing of this record has been scored, no forecast of it frozen.
parent_record: prereg/addenda_wiki_led/2026-11-26_o_transformer_inputs_check.json and its parents. Rows (1,258,807 scored work-format-months, origins 2019-01 to 2026-07), target D, history, calendar and own-page features (W14C), the 35 plain 60-month loan features C (o01_controls.py, feat_C.parquet), LightGBM settings, walk-forward by test year 2019 to 2026, five seeds 20261020 to 20261024, change rank, the 2,000 draws of 3-month blocks (rng 20261020), the 14 families of kinds of book, the too-small rule, Benjamini-Hochberg within each comparison and the wording rule are addendum o's (o02_models.py, o04_score.py, which copies n50_score.py) unless changed here.
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai. After addendum o Claude said the 5-year loan history should not become the main model before checking whether Wikipedia still helps on top of it, and asked "Run the check of Wikipedia's gain on top of 5 years of loans?"; Khant answered "Yes, run it" on 26 Nov 2026.
why: In addendum o the plain 60 months of loans (C) added +0.0128 to HMW14 (library history plus own and author pages), more than anything else so far, so it is a candidate for the main library model. The Wikipedia gain of the thesis (HMW14 minus HM, about +0.005) was measured on top of a history that reaches back about 12 months. Part of what the pages carry (for example which books stay read for years) may also be in older loans, so the Wikipedia gain could shrink once the model sees 5 years. The scored review of 26 Nov also asked for the strongest library model as the reference.
models: LightGBM as addendum o. New: HM60 = HM + C (the 9 history and calendar features plus the 35 plain 60-month features; no Wikipedia feature). Stored: HM, HMW14 (addendum l, five seeds, n's preds) and HMW14C = HMW14 + C (addendum o, o02). So HMW14C minus HM60 is the Wikipedia gain on top of 5 years of loans, with the same rows, seeds and settings. Check: a refit of HM for the first test year must equal the stored HM predictions (as o02).

samples.all_books: All 1,258,807 scored rows, as addendum o.
samples.books_with_a_page: Rows whose work has its own Wikipedia article or whose author has one (has_book_page or has_author_page in the rows, as p03_page_books_scores.py), the sample of the 26 Nov direction. Books are ranked against each other within these rows only (format x month cells), not within all books.

tests.Q1_all_books: HMW14C minus HM60 change rank, all books, all scored months 2019 to 2026, addendum o's draws.
tests.Q2_books_with_a_page: HMW14C minus HM60 change rank on books with a page, ranked within them, all scored months 2019 to 2026, the same draws.
tests.decision: Holm over Q1 and Q2 at one-sided 0.05; a test passes if Holm rejects it, its estimate is above 0 and its 95% interval is above 0. Wording: if a test passes, 'the Wikipedia pages still help [sample] once the model has 5 years of loans'; if not, 'their help is not clear once the model has 5 years of loans'. Choosing the main model stays Khant's; this record only says which comparisons hold.
tests.Q3_blind_month: Frozen forecasts at origin 2026-08 for target 2026-09 of HM60 (five-seed mean, fitted on every row with target month up to 2026-08, as o03), in prereg/blind_q/, SHA-256 in prereg/README.md and public before any month after 2026-08 is downloaded; HMW14C's are already frozen in prereg/blind_o/. Check: seed 20261020's HM refit on the same rows equals addendum l's frozen HM_D (difference below 1e-6). Scored once, after l06_score.py's final run has built world_2026-09, with o06_blind_score.py's measures (change rank within format averaged over formats; paired bootstrap over works, 2,000 draws, seed 20261126). Decision: HMW14C minus HM60 change rank with a 95% interval above 0, for all books and for books with a page, each read on its own; one month is a small test.
tests.descriptive_no_rule: HM60 minus HM (what 5 years of loans add without Wikipedia); HMW14 minus HM (the Wikipedia gain on top of about 12 months, for the same rows); the share of that gain left on top of 5 years, (HMW14C - HM60) / (HMW14 - HM), from five-seed means inside each draw; the difference of the two Wikipedia gains; both samples by format and for 2024 to 2026; books with their own article and books with an author article only (as p03); monthly top-20 and early-warning lists; by kind of book, HMW14C minus HM60 over the 14 families, Benjamini-Hochberg, too-small rule.

order_of_work: 1 this record, fingerprinted and public before any step; 2 HM60 walk-forward, five seeds; 3 HM60 frozen forecasts for 2026-09; 4 scoring and report; 5 code, frozen forecasts and results in a pull request; 6 later, once September 2026 is downloaded, the blind score. Nothing is rerun after a result except to fix a logged coding error.
seen_before_fixing: All addendum o results (HM 0.347, HMW14 0.352, HMW14C 0.365, C added to HMW14 +0.0128, all books); its segments table, which holds HMW14C's score in each kind-of-book group, including the own-article groups (book article, author article only, neither); the page-books scores of p03 (HM 0.348 to HMW14 0.355 on books with a page). Not computed before fixing: HM60 in any form, HMW14C on books with a page as one sample, any Wikipedia gain on top of C.
known_limits: C is one fair plain use of 60 months of loans, not every possible one; a longer or different history could shrink the Wikipedia gain further. The blind month is one month. Books with no loan history (new books) are not in these rows; their test is separate. Results describe this library and these books.
